subject: Film & Cinema
title: Color Grading: The Digital Paintbrush
description: A fast breakdown of Color Grading: The Digital Paintbrush for builders.

hook.text: The teal-and-orange look of modern blockbusters wasn't filmed that way. It was graded.

buildup.text: Color grading adjusts hues, saturation, and contrast to create a film's final visual identity.

discovery.text: O Brother, Where Art Thou? was the first film entirely color-graded digitally, creating sepia warmth.

twist.text: Heavy grading can make films look artificial — the orange-and-teal trend has exhausted audiences.

climax.text: The colorist is cinema's least-known essential artist — they paint the final emotional layer.

punchline.text: The last brush stroke changes everything.

quiz.question: What was the first film entirely color-graded digitally?
